title: Native-shell and Telegram-mini-app absences
why: Three rows recording that neither of these two "channels" is one this repository can build or verify. S-455 is not merely missing source: the schemes (`mayaos` / `ru.mayaos.app` / `pro.malesthetic.app`), the MayaRuntime / MayaNfcWriter / MayaVoiceRecorder / TeamVoicePlayer plugin implementations, the AppIconBarber asset, `launchAutoHide=false` and the APNs entitlements all live in the external maya-ios checkout (AGENTS.md:13-15), so a chat-first change that renames a scheme, drops a plugin call or reorders boot passes every check here and still bricks the shipped app; the Android TWA package and keystore are absent too, so Android cannot be rebuilt here at all. S-488 is the consequential one: `telegram-web-app.js` is never loaded (0 hits repo-wide; `app.html` carries no `script src` tags at all), so if that absence holds in production every `window.Telegram && window.Telegram.WebApp &&` guard falls through to the `window.__tgAuthData` / `web_session_token` branches, giving Mini App users no automatic role resolution (contradicting bot.py:4256-4258), no foreign-login eviction, and payment links that open in-place — all failing quietly, which is why it survived. None of the three rows is a primary-nav entry, so the collapse of 101 primary-nav entries to 5 does not touch them; all three name no capability on the inventory row and are marked REQUIRES SIGNATURE, which is exactly what you are signing here.
disappear: Only the orphaned stylesheet `native-styles.css` (S-481), retired row by row in K16. It is confirmed dead on both axes — 0 inbound references from any `*.html` and 0 in `docs/`, so it is not even present in the deployed edge inventory — and retiring it removes no capability. The one care named on the row is not to resurrect it as a second source of native chrome alongside the live `html.me-web-desktop` rules at app.html:42.
remain: The recorded absence of native source (S-455) stays as a release-authority boundary: retired as UI in K15 with the fence server-side, carried as a mirror obligation against the external maya-ios checkout, because nothing in this repository can prove a chat-first change is safe for the shipped iOS app and Android cannot be rebuilt here at all. The Telegram mini-app identity contract (S-488) stays explicitly unresolved and must be settled before the identity redesign — settled against the live https://malesthetic.pro/app/index.html, not against this bundle — and until it is, no conversational onboarding may be designed on "Telegram already knows who you are". Both S-455 and S-488 carry the same parity requirement: the fence fires independently of any UI, proved by test. All three owner cells still require your signature, since no capability is named on any of the three inventory rows.
risk: MEDIUM — but read as a present-tense finding, not as a prerequisite for later work. If S-488's absence holds in production, Mini App users today get no automatic role resolution (contradicting bot.py:4256-4258), no foreign-login eviction, and payment links that open in-place, all failing silently. S-455 means a chat-first change that renames a scheme, drops a MayaRuntime / MayaNfcWriter / MayaVoiceRecorder / TeamVoicePlayer call, or reorders boot will pass every check in this repository and still brick the shipped app, with Android unbuildable here at all. The level stays MEDIUM because signing these three cells changes nothing in production: both hazards are recorded, not created, and S-488's production effect is stated conditionally and has not been checked against the live https://malesthetic.pro/app/index.html. S-488 is the one row in this group that must be settled before the identity redesign begins.
user_impact: Only one of the three rows is invisible to everyone, and it is not the two the entry names. S-481 is genuinely dead: `grep -rn --include='*.html' native-styles` returns 0 inbound references (the 2803-byte file is still on disk at `сайт и приложение/native-styles.css`), so nobody can reach a rule in it today. S-455 is NOT invisible — it is a blind spot over users who exist. `AGENTS.md:13-15` names a shipped iOS Capacitor app (`/Users/stanislavmosin/Desktop/maya-ios`, `ios/App/App.xcodeproj`) and the Android TWA package/keystore is likewise absent here (`find` over *.swift/*.kt/*.java/*.pbxproj/AndroidManifest.xml/capacitor.config.*/Info.plist and over *.keystore/*.jks both return 0 in the canonical repo). Those people are running a shell this repo cannot see: a chat-first change that renames a scheme, drops a MayaRuntime/MayaNfcWriter/MayaVoiceRecorder/TeamVoicePlayer plugin call or reorders boot will pass every check here and still brick the app in their hands, and Android cannot be rebuilt from this repo at all. That is a user-facing blast radius carried as a mirror obligation, not "not a screen anyone taps." S-488 is the row that touches a person directly, and it is stronger than stated: `ai администратор/bot.py:4256-4266` sets a Telegram Mini App menu button ("Приложение" → https://malesthetic.pro/app/index.html?v=2) on every bot start, and the comment directly above it asserts the exact fiction — "Telegram автоматически передаёт их аккаунт (initData) — роль ... определяется сама, без ввода номера и Login Widget". The bundle contradicts that comment: `app.html` has 0 `<script src>` tags, its only dynamic script injection is jsQR (`app.html:35792`), and `telegram-web-app.js` appears 0 times repo-wide, so `window.Telegram.WebApp` is never defined and every guarded path falls through. The fallback is not smooth: it is the deep-link applogin flow (`app.html:41114-41135`) that pushes the person out of the mini app into the bot chat with `?start=app_<nonce>` and polls for a `web_session_token`. So a client or staff member who taps the bot's own "Приложение" button today gets a sign-in detour instead of automatic role resolution; the rebuild does not change that, it records it — which is why chat-first onboarding must not be written as though Telegram already knows who the person is. Verified in the repo bundle and bot.py only; not checked against the deployed https://malesthetic.pro/app/index.html.
security_impact: Direction is right — nothing load-bearing is removed, no new server-side check is created, and S-488 documents a gap that is already open rather than opening one — but "neutral overall" undersells what S-488 records. S-481 retires a stylesheet with 0 inbound references and removes no capability (the only care is not resurrecting it beside the live `html.me-web-desktop` rules at app.html:42). S-455 changes no authority check, but state the consequence plainly: with 0 native sources and 0 keystores in-tree, release/signing authority is not merely "a mirror obligation" by preference — it is unprovable here, so no repo gate can ever enforce it and it must be written as an explicit external obligation. S-488 is the real security content. The six `X-Telegram-InitData` headers in app.html are all behind the `window.Telegram && window.Telegram.WebApp` guard and never fire, so the server never receives initData for this channel at all — there is no Telegram-verified identity to "keep as the sole authority"; what must stay authoritative is the session/auth_data verification the server already performs. And the residual exposure is not neutral: identity here does not rest solely on the server-issued session token. `hasSession()` also accepts a persisted `tg_auth_data` Login-Widget payload for up to 30 days (`app.html:41331`) with no live cross-check, while `__meDropForeignLogin()` — the anti-impersonation eviction — returns early whenever `initDataUnsafe.user.id` is missing (`app.html:41371-41372`), i.e. always. The bundle's own comment at `app.html:41334-41338` concedes this ("`__meDropForeignLogin` ничего не делает (нет Telegram initDataUnsafe)") and names `__meClearIdentityCache()` on each fresh login as the compensating control — which does not run on a shared device where nobody logs out. So the row preserves a live stale-identity/credential-persistence exposure that the rebuild inherits and must close server-side; it does not create it, and it contradicts none of the frozen limitations (fail-closed 13/21, STEP_UP unreachable, Gate 10 measured not enforced, approval role-gated not separation-of-duties, GAP-ATTENDANCE-CONFIRM open are all untouched by this group).
